All agenda items and reports are available for review in the City Clerk’s Office and
www.hpca.gov. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding
any item on this agenda (other than writings legally exempt from public disclosure) will be
made available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk located at 6550 Miles
Avenue, Huntington Park, California 90255 during regular business hours, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30
p.m., Monday – Thursday, and at the City Hall Council Chambers during the meeting.

Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, including
auxiliary aids or services, in order to participate in the public meeting may request such
modification, accommodation, aid or service by contacting the City Clerk’s Office either in
person at 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California or by telephone at (323) 584-6230.
Notification in advance of the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements
to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

PLEASE SILENCE ALL CELL PHONES AND OTHER ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT
WHILE COUNCIL IS IN SESSION. Thank you.

PLEASE NOTE-The numerical order of items on this agenda is for convenience of reference.
Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City Council.
Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order and
decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
 July 28, 2026  Page 1 of 3
  the City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.
  • The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code, commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park
  City Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each speaker
  will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed on the City
  Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct disruptive
  to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of Procedure or
  conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must be
  directed to the mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required for
the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

PUBLIC COMMENT

For both open and closed sessions, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per
Huntington Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other
speakers and may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one
meeting to another. This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled
public hearing items.

All comments or queries should be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown
Act, no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing
on the posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide
direction to staff, or schedule a matter for a future meeting.

  1. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING

  2. Take public testimony;

  as a special assessment to be collected at the same time and in the
  manner as county taxes. The motion was seconded Councilmember
  Flores. The motion was carried by unanimous consent.

  2. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING AND
  ORDERING THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF THE ANNUAL SPECIAL TAX FOR
  THE CITY OF HUNTINGTON PARK STREET LIGHTING, PARKS, AND
  LANDSCAPING SPECIAL TAX DISTRICT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1.  Conduct a public hearing;

  2.  Take public testimony; and

  3.  Adopt Resolution No. 2026-40, Establishing and Ordering the Levy and
  Collection of the Annual Special Tax for the City of Huntington Park Street
  Lighting, Parks and Landscaping Special Tax District for Fiscal Year 2026-
  2027.
   Public Hearing Opened: 6:34pm

  Rodolfo Cruz

  Public Hearing Closed: 6:38pm

  MOTION:  Councilmember Martiz expressed her concerns stating that lighting is
  necessary in the City of Huntington Park. Mayor Martinez mentioned
  his concerns regarding lighting at Veterans Park. Councilmember
  Flores expressed his concerns about how the funding was approved
  with the notion that the bulk of the funding raised would be spent on
  lighting not landscaping. Mayor Martinez motioned to approve the
  Item with the amendment to allocate more funding towards lighting
  not landscaping. The motion was seconded by Councilmember
  Flores. The motion was carried by unanimous vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Macias, Flores, Vice Mayor Sanabria,
  and Mayor Martinez.

  NOES:  Council Member(s): None

  ABSTAIN:  Council Member(s): None

CITY MANAGER

  3. INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE 4 OF
  THE HUNTINGTON PARK MUNICIPAL CODE REGARDING THE REMOVAL OF
  THE CITY MANAGER

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Conduct a public hearing;

  2. Introduce, by title only, and waive further reading of the proposed ordinance
  amending Chapter 2, Article 4 of the Huntington Park Municipal Code regarding
  the removal of the City Manager; and

  3. Direct staff to return the ordinance for second reading and adoption.

  Public Hearing Opened: 6:45pm

  Rodolfo Cruz

  Public Hearing Closed: 6:47pm

  MOTION:  Councilmember Flores stated that he supports the transition. Vice
  Mayor Sanabria stated that he also supports the protection for the
  City Manager. Councilmember Martiz stated the importance of
  retaining professionals. Councilmember Martiz stated how councils
  are temporary. Mayor Martinez states how he supports the motion.
  Councilmember Martiz stated that performance review should be
  taken into consideration when planning for succession. City Attorney
  explained the interim/ acting City Manager appointment process.
  Vice Mayor Sanabria motioned to Introduce, by title only, and waive
  further reading of the proposed ordinance amending Chapter 2,
  Article 4 of the Huntington Park Municipal Code regarding the
  removal of the City Manager; and direct staff to return the ordinance
  for second reading and adoption. The motion was seconded by
  Councilmember Flores. Councilmember Macias motioned against
  the motion. The motion was carried by majority vote.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Martiz, Flores, Vice Mayor Sanabria, and
  Mayor Martinez.

   REPORTS AND INFORMATIONAL ITEMS

PUBLIC WORKS

1.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF MOU TO ENTER  INTO
  PARTNERSHIPWITH TREEPEOPLE FOR TREE PLANTING PROGRAM

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the City of
  Huntington Park and Tree People to continue their partnership on a U.S. Forest
  Service-funded tree planting program.

  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve the MOU and any related documents
  necessary to implement the agreement and carry out the tree planting program
  in accordance with its terms.

  MOTION:  Councilmember Flores motioned to approve the Memorandum of
  Understanding (MOU) between the City of Huntington Park and Tree
  People to continue their partnership on a U.S. Forest Service-funded
  tree planting program and authorize the City Manager to approve the
  MOU and any related documents necessary to implement the
  agreement and carry out the tree planting program in accordance
  with its terms. The motion was seconded by Councilmember Martiz.
  The motion was carried by unanimous consent.

  DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

City Manager: Take a second to welcome our Interim City Clerk Pat Jacquez- Nares.

City Attorney: No Report.

Public Works: No Report

Community Development: No Report

Police: No Report

Finance: No Report

City Clerk: No Report

Parks and Rec: Friday, August 7th we will be kicking off our summer night’s events.
Saturday, August 8th we will be hosting our back-to-school event at Salt Lake Park, where
we’ll be giving backpacks. Friday, August 14th will be movie night at Salt Lake Park.

Communication: Good Evening. National Night Out will be taking place on Tuesday,
August 4th at 5pm at Freedom Park. We will also continue to have the program “Run with
Us” at the high school track. We invite the community to run with us on Saturdays that is
open at 8am. The city will be hosting another back-to-school event on August 13th from 2-
4pm with “HP with You” at Freedom Park. We will also be having a Civic Leadership
Academy program, it will be 6 weeks, and we include sessions for individuals to learn
about how the city functions.
 WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

Councilmember Martiz: She wanted to give some feedback. She attended the public
workshop and got feedback regarding the 5K. There was a lot of feedback in terms of
the route. As we organize the 5K, we are partnered with an organization that can
produce a very good 5K for the members of the public. She provided some of that
feedback, but as we think about the route we should take into consideration portable
restrooms. There is opportunity to reach out to the community leaders and deliver
something that our residents would like. She would also like to provide feedback on the
Civic Leadership Workshop. She would like it to be approachable to all members of the
public, not just individuals with an interest in government or in the field of public
administration. If possible, she would like to add a theme to the workshops, this allows
different departments to focus on one aspect per department and allows our residents to
become more engaged.

Councilmember Macias: She wished everybody a good evening.

Councilmember Flores: He welcomed Interim City Clerk Pat Jacquez- Nares. If we
could get an HR report of all the vacancies in the city in various departments it would be
appreciated.

Vice Mayor Sanabria: Thank you staff for all the work that you have done.

Mayor Martinez: Thank you for making sure we are here safe. Thank you for posting all
the events on social media. That means the city is doing good providing excellent
resources to the members of the community.
